Because a majority of people receive much of their care out-
side the hospital, regular nutrition assessment and monitoring 
are important. The HCT procedure is associated with severe 
nutritional consequences that require prompt, proactive inter-
vention. Nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea are caused by the cyto-
toxic conditioning regimen and may later accompany antibiotic 
administration. Complications of delayed-onset nutrition- 
related symptoms include varying degrees of mucositis, xero-
stomia, and dysgeusia. Mucositis, which is often severe and ex-
tremely painful, develops in more than 75% of transplant 
patients (see Figure 36-2).

CHAPTER 36  Medical Nutrition Therapy for Cancer Prevention, Treatment
Nutritional Precautions with Neutropenia
Individuals receiving HCT become immunocompromised and 
require supportive therapy, including medications and dietary 
changes to prevent infection. Some cancer centers continue to 
prescribe a low-microbial or low-bacteria diet for people with 
low white blood cell counts (neutropenia). However, there is no 
clear evidence that a strict “neutropenic” diet (only cooked 
foods) reduces overall rates of infection or death (AND, EAL,
